_why: What the layout guard renders the screens with.
It exists because of ledger 149: the guard started a daemon with an empty
data directory, so every screen that shows rows showed none, and /kubernetes
reported '3 controls' for a page that carries a dozen. A guard that measures
the empty state passes the exact screen the operator photographed as broken.
The values are deliberately LONG. A short hostname fits anywhere; what breaks
a phone layout is 'srv-rsp-prod01.holzcloud.ch', a pod called
'coredns-7c65d6cfc9-x4m2p' and an image reference with a registry in front of
it. Fixtures made of 'foo' and 'bar' would measure a layout nobody has.
web/src/fixtures.test.ts parses every entry below with the SAME zod schema
the product parses the server's answer with, so these cannot drift into a
shape the app would reject -- which would leave the guard measuring an error
page and calling it a clean run.

/api/v1/clusters/c-homelab/kubernetes/sw.notice: Only things that have finished and are not the way back from a rollout. Running, pending and unknown pods are left alone -- unknown especially, because that means a node stopped reporting rather than that the pod stopped. Images on the nodes are not here: Talos cannot delete one, and the kubelet removes them itself when its disk fills.

volumes.name: pvc-11b7e004-longhorn-old-grafana-storage

claims.name: prometheus-server-storage
claims.notice: Its class waits for a consumer, so it stays Pending until a pod that uses it is scheduled. That is the class working as configured, not a fault.

/api/v1/clusters/c-homelab/kubernetes/st.notice: A capacity here is what was provisioned, not how full the filesystem on it is: nothing in the Kubernetes API reports that, and only something running inside the pod can. A volume’s reclaim policy is what decides whether deleting its claim destroys the data.

/api/v1/clusters/c-homelab/kubernetes/ne.notice: Endpoints are counted from EndpointSlices, which is what the kube-proxy on each node actually load-balances to. A Service with none refuses every connection instantly, and nothing else about it looks wrong.

/api/v1/clusters/c-homelab/kubernetes/ac.notice: A binding that names a role or a service account which does not exist grants nothing, and looks exactly like one that works: RBAC has no referential integrity, deliberately, so that a binding may be written before its role. Administrative means wildcard verbs on wildcard resources, whatever the role is called -- looking for the name cluster-admin would miss every hand-written role with the same power.

namespaces.name: monitoring
namespaces.notice: It has a quota on cpu or memory and no LimitRange, so every pod that does not set requests itself is refused -- not for being too big, but because the quota cannot account for a pod that asked for nothing. The error says "must specify limits", which reads as the pod being wrong.

custom_kinds.notice: The API server is not serving this kind, so every manifest naming it is refused. A definition waits like this while its conversion webhook is unreachable.

/api/v1/clusters/c-homelab/kubernetes/in.notice: A quota’s used figure is what the namespace has reserved, and a full quota is why the next pod is refused -- the pod’s own event says "exceeded quota" and nothing else shows the quota. Objects of the cluster’s own kinds are not counted here: that would be one list call per kind, and a cluster can have two hundred.
